title: St. Joseph's Night, the Indians and Mardi Gras bands
summary: Punch describes Mardi Gras Indians who clashed with each other, the many bands and the parade routes.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about St. Joseph's Night at the Indians. Oh, here?

Yeah. Well, yeah, I'll tell you something about that. I never played no dance. I played dance on that, but what I mean, it wasn't just some people in Mass and come to the dance and dance, you know. But I mean, two of them like, be up and down the street, like on Marty Roddy. But did Mass all right, did Mass and come to the dance. The Indians would dress up? Well, different ones, the Indians, what do you call them, the other ones, the Yallapocahomans and all of them would come, you know, dancing. But the most time you wouldn't hardly see the Indians and the Yallapocahomans meet. If the Indians would go there, the Yallapocahomans would go over there, because they couldn't get along. They couldn't get along.
How many bands would they have out on a Mardi Gras day, you figure?

Well, no, I can't tell you, but I could say in them times, they used to have like, well, the Whitehead bands too, I couldn't count them, but I knew they'd have about seven or eight colored bands, brass bands, and some on wagons with orchestras, you know, playing on wagons, you know. There was lots of them out there. Everybody could play some of them, was, out that day, you know, playing.
Would they come up in the neighborhoods, or would they stay on St. Charles and go around?

Man, all through, everywhere you were, St. Charles, around. All right, you got a club, you see, my brother is sitting to the place. I go down St. Charles to St. St. Street, go out to St. St. Street, go down to St. St. Street, hit downtown. You might come across, hit Ramport Street, come to Connell, then go out to Connell to the river. Another group, go another way, you know. You know, it's all over town, you see.
That's the way King Zulu was patterned his road, he's all over the city.
